content: The treatment involves administering 40 mg of pantoprazole orally once daily for 8 to 16 weeks. For maintenance of healing, the same dose of 40 mg orally once daily is recommended. Alternatively, 40 mg can be given intravenously once daily for 7 to 10 days if oral therapy is not feasible. In cases where oral administration is not possible, 40 mg can be infused intravenously over 15 minutes once daily for 7 to 10 days, with a switch to oral therapy (40 mg daily) as soon as the patient can swallow. In some patients, up to 240 mg per day may be administered, with 80 mg given via IV infusion every 8 to 12 hours for up to 7 days, followed by a switch to oral therapy when feasible. For duodenal ulcers, 40 mg orally once daily for 2 weeks is recommended. For gastric ulcers, 40 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks is advised. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of erlotinib by altering the pH of the upper gastrointestinal tract, which reduces erlotinib's solubility and bioavailability. Concomitant use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) with erlotinib should be avoided if possible. Pantoprazole increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. This can lead to increased systemic exposure to mavacamten, potentially causing heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. Concomitant use is contraindicated. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of nelfinavir through an unspecified interaction mechanism, likely involving CYP2C19 inhibition and reduced gastric pH, which decreases nelfinavir absorption. This coadministration is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and resistance development. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH, which can lead to treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is contraindicated. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces acalabrutinib solubility. Due to the long-lasting effect of PPIs, separating doses may not eliminate the interaction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pantoprazole increases the levels or effects of alpelisib by inhibiting BCRP metabolism, which may increase the risk of toxicities. If coadministration is unavoidable, closely monitor for adverse reactions. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of pantoprazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. This interaction may result in lower exposure to pantoprazole. Avoid or substitute another drug when possible. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces atazanavir solubility. Substantially reduced plasma concentrations of atazanavir are expected if PPIs are coadministered. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pantoprazole increases the levels or effects of digoxin by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of itraconazole and ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH, which reduces their solubility. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pantoprazole increases the levels of cannabidiol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider reducing the dose of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates when coadministered with cannabidiol. Pantoprazole decreases the effects of capecitabine by an unknown mechanism, potentially impairing tablet dissolution and/or reducing absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of ceritinib by increasing gastric pH. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Pantoprazole increases the toxicity of cilostazol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider decreasing the cilostazol dose. Pantoprazole decreases the effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism, which reduces the conversion of clopidogrel to its active metabolite. Use caution and monitor closely. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces velpatasvir solubility. Coadministration with PPIs is not recommended. If necessary, administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with food 4 hours before omeprazole 20 mg. Pantoprazole increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting BCRP metabolism. If coadministration cannot be avoided, monitor for potential adverse reactions. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of bosutinib by approximately 45% due to its pH-dependent solubility. Use caution and monitor closely. Pantoprazole decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which may cause premature dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Pantoprazole increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting BCRP metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects when coadministered. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Use caution and monitor closely. Pantoprazole increases the levels of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and reduce the dose of CYP2C19 substrates as clinically appropriate. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of mesalamine by increasing gastric pH, which affects the dissolution of sustained-release dosage forms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pantoprazole increases the levels of riociguat by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if needed. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH, which may reduce its efficacy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pantoprazole increases the levels of sotagliflozin by inhibiting BCRP metabolism. Monitor for potential adverse reactions. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration with drugs that raise gastric pH. Use short-acting antacids as an alternative. Pantoprazole increases the levels of ozanimod by inhibiting BCRP metabolism, which increases the exposure of its active metabolites. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of pexidartinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration with PPIs. Use H2-receptor antagonists or antacids if needed. Pantoprazole increases the levels of atogepant by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of belumosudil by increasing gastric pH. Increase the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg twice daily when coadministered with PPIs. Pantoprazole increases the levels of cenobamate by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider a dose reduction of CYP2C19 substrates when used concomitantly with cenobamate. Pantoprazole increases the levels of cilostazol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider decreasing the cilostazol dose. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
